ruler.name: King Rasiq ben Tumek
ruler.bio: Rasiq ben Tumek is a Khadi chosen by the well-lords after his uncle's death, and he rules the northern desert, the Salt Road and the tribes of the Moco and Mylunur from Furvior. He is a careful king who keeps the Powder Refusal sworn at the Seven Wells, so that no rider of Noris carries black powder, and he fights the rivalry with Stabilo in tolls, bribes and caravan prices, playing its great houses against each other. The generous friends of the Deliverer's temple at Furvior have lent him more than his treasurers like to admit.

portrait.appearance: A lean, sun-browned desert king with kohl-rimmed eyes and a short greying beard.
portrait.dress: An indigo robe and veil-cloth thrown back from the face, a camel-hair cloak, a silver well-seal on a cord.
portrait.colours: Desert indigo (#2b3f7a), dune gold (#c9964a), sand pale (#efe3c4).

ruler.formerName: King Esiurth II of Noris (characters spec and the Noris tree; superseded by the histories)

heir.name: Zarud ben Tumek
heir.role: The king's younger brother, a rider of the border wells who thinks the Powder Refusal is a fine oath and a poor plan.
heir.succession: The well-lords choose the king from the Khadi line; a king who loses their trust is left without riders.
heir.portrait: A young rider in indigo with a lance and a hawk on his arm.

advisors.name: Alodar Kersi, Master of Caravans
advisors.role: Sets the salt and dye caravans on the road and knows the price of every camel between Furvior and Duum-Saah.
advisors.portrait: A caravan master in sand-coloured robes with three sets of scales.

advisors.name: Nurqas, Star-Reader of the Seven Wells
advisors.role: Noris's named wise man, of a well-lord's line, who reads the stars for the caravans of the Salt Road and finds water where there is water to find; he distrusts the temples of every city.
advisors.portrait: An old desert sage with a brass star-table and a white veil.
advisors.secret: His distrust of the temples is right (A); no text says so before zin_afrit_revealed.

advisors.name: Well-Lord Melud ben Yakar
advisors.role: Eldest of the well-lords who chose the king, and the first to leave a king without riders if he loses their trust.
advisors.portrait: A white-bearded well-lord with a water-skin and a staff.

advisors.name: Khadiq ben Furud, Keeper of the Treasury
advisors.role: Keeps the king's treasury and the list of what the temple's friends have lent, which he keeps shorter than it is.
advisors.portrait: A stout treasurer with a locked chest and an abacus.

advisors.name: Qasar ben Melek, Master of the Riders
advisors.role: Keeps the camel herds and the tribes' riders, and swears no powder-engine ever caught a camel.
advisors.portrait: A hawk-faced rider-captain with a curved sword and an indigo turban.

advisors.name: Alodim ben Furud, Envoy to Duum-Saah
advisors.role: Keeps the Noris Treaty in good repair at the court of Naamis, and is the treasurer's brother, which is useful to them both.
advisors.portrait: A poised man in indigo and gold with a treaty-case.

commanders.name: Rider-General Tumo Furan
commanders.role: Has led the border riders for thirty years and never lost a well.
commanders.portrait: A rider-general with a veil and a lance on a white camel.

commanders.name: Zarim ben Qasud of the Border Wells
commanders.role: Leads the riders of the border wells and raids Stabilo's caravans when the king pretends not to notice.
commanders.portrait: A young camel-rider with a red sash and a short bow.

commanders.name: Alod ben Rasud of the Salt Road
commanders.office: Captain of the Salt Road Guard
commanders.role: Guards the Salt Road from Furvior to the sea and knows the water at every stage of it.
commanders.portrait: A veiled rider-captain with a lance and a string of water-skins.

ruler.name: Prince Pleron Tablo
ruler.bio: Pleron Tablo was a banker before he was a prince, and the bench of houses chose him for life because he knows every house's debts. He governs the Gold Road, the southern hills and the old caravan towns from Postondoroth, the largest city of the East, whose powder-engines and hired companies make it the strongest purse in the region. He believes the East can be ruled by ledgers without a single war, which is an easy thing to believe with ledgers as full as his, and several of his great houses owe the Deliverer's temple more than the bench has been told.

portrait.appearance: An olive-skinned, smooth-shaven banker-prince with heavy-lidded, calculating eyes.
portrait.dress: A robe of oxblood silk with a jewelled collar, the golden scales of the Prince on a chain, a signet with the Tablo mark.

ruler.formerName: Prince Cereos of Postondoroth (characters spec; superseded by the histories)

heir.name: Demano Fundo
heir.office: Head of the House of Fundo
heir.role: Head of the house of Fundo, descendant of the Demio who made the Peace of Cereosa, and the bench's likeliest choice when the seat falls empty.
heir.succession: The bench of houses chooses the Prince of the Scales for life from among the great houses.
heir.portrait: A grave merchant in green silk with the Fundo mark.

advisors.name: Lord Arcar Azano, Treasurer of the Pact
advisors.role: A cousin of the house that owns Ceralon, who keeps the Stabilo Pact's treasury and whose books are better kept than the bench's.
advisors.portrait: A treasurer with scales and seals, in amber silk.
advisors.formerName: Lord Mylun Azano (characters spec and the Stabilo tree; renamed because Mylana Azano rules Azano in the histories)

advisors.name: Weigher Arcio Prudo of the Hall of Scales
advisors.office: Master Weigher of the Hall of Scales
advisors.role: Judges contracts in the Hall of Scales, where a false weight is the worst crime in Stabilo, and has never found a Prudo guilty of one.
advisors.portrait: A stern weigher in a black robe beside a great bronze scale.

advisors.name: Demeo Dolgio, Master of the Wall-Engines
advisors.role: Keeps the powder-engines on the harbour walls of Postondoroth and the crews hired to use them; he is a cousin of the Drak forge-masters and talks shop with them by every post.
advisors.portrait: A soot-marked engine-master with a match-cord and a brass measuring rod.

advisors.name: Magister Cereo Shindia
advisors.role: Stabilo's named practitioner, a merchant-magister of the essence-smiths who quenches the companies' iron and argues with the star-readers of Noris by letter.
advisors.portrait: A man in a scorched silk apron with essence-vials at his belt.

advisors.name: Arcino Prudo, Speaker for the Great Houses
advisors.role: Speaks for the great houses on the bench, several of which owe the temple's generous friends rather more than they have said.
advisors.portrait: An elegant man in jade silk with a ledger and a sealed loan.

advisors.name: Belano Ceron, Master of the Harbour
advisors.office: Master of the Harbour of Postondoroth
advisors.role: Keeps the harbour and the galleys of Postondoroth, and the engines on the walls stand over his ships.
advisors.portrait: A harbour-master in an amber coat with a brass speaking-trumpet.

commanders.name: Captain-General Hardfic Shindor
commanders.role: Has led hired companies for forty years and never broken a contract; his house is paid in advance.
commanders.portrait: A grizzled captain-general in bronze scale.

commanders.name: Captain Nareo Tablon of the Crossbows
commanders.role: Commands the bronze-armoured crossbow companies who hold the Gold Road junctions.
commanders.portrait: A bronze-armoured captain with a crossbow on his back.

commanders.name: Captain Belo Fundo of the Engine Crews
commanders.role: Leads the companies trained to the powder-engines in the field and is the only Fundo who prefers a costly victory to a good peace.
commanders.portrait: A sharp-faced man in a leather coat with a match-cord.

commanders.name: Sea-Captain Posio Cerano
commanders.role: Commands the galleys that carry the Gold Road's goods along the coast and keep the Noris Treaty's ships honest.
commanders.portrait: A galley captain in amber with a bronze helm.

ruler.name: King Kerseus Furanides
ruler.bio: Kerseus Furanides was crowned standing in the Rising twelve floods ago, as every Furanid king has been, and every proclamation calls him Alerh after the river. He rules the great river valley on the rift from the stair-city of Porrenva, an old crown rich in grain and scribes, neutral between Noris and Stabilo, and he looks across the Rift Narrows at the elven shore his kings have traded with for three ages. His scribe-council distrusts the caravan princes and borrows from them all the same.

portrait.appearance: A tall, olive-skinned king with painted eyes and a carefully curled black beard.
portrait.dress: A white linen robe with a broad gold collar, the river-crown of reeds and gold, wet to the knee from the Rising.
portrait.colours: River gold (#c9a24a), flood blue (#2f5f8a), reed green (#4a7a4a).

heir.name: Prince Kerseion Furanides
heir.role: The king's eldest son, who has been taught by the scribes and will stand in the Rising when his turn comes.
heir.succession: Hereditary in the Furanides; the new king is crowned standing in the Rising.
heir.portrait: A boy-prince in white linen with a small gold collar.

advisors.name: Chief Scribe Alerhan Alerhos
advisors.role: Leads the scribe-council that has signed Alerhia's treaties since the first Aenoran traders came, and distrusts every caravan prince on principle.
advisors.portrait: A grey-haired scribe with a reed pen behind his ear and a roll of papyrus.

advisors.name: Thareon of the Stair
advisors.role: Climbs the stair-temples to the River and the Kings Below each year, and seats the twelve as guests at the top step.
advisors.portrait: An old priest in white on a temple stair with a bowl of river water.

advisors.name: Furanian Kalis, Keeper of the Granaries
advisors.role: Keeps the granaries of the river valley and the loans from the caravan princes, which he hopes the scribes never add up.
advisors.portrait: A plump official with a grain-measure and a gold collar.

commanders.name: Rhanion of the Chariots
commanders.role: Commands the chariots and archers of the river crown, who have not fought a real war since the Stair Peace and drill as though they had.
commanders.portrait: A charioteer in a gilded corselet with a long bow.

commanders.name: Alerh of the River Fleet
commanders.role: Commands the river galleys from Porrenva to the rift and the ships that carry grain to the elven quays.
commanders.portrait: A river-captain in blue linen at the steering oar.

ruler.name: Queen Shinah bat Alodar
ruler.bio: Shinah bat Alodar rules the sea crown of the north coast plain from Duum-Saah with the council of ship-masters, who may refuse her ships but not her crown. The Noris Treaty is the pillar of her policy, and her ships carry the Salt Road's salt, dye and camel-hair cloth along the coast and into the North Mouth of the Rift. She listens with unease when the island fishers tell of strange ships among the black isles of the Kusmeel, and unlike the other courts she has not laughed.

portrait.appearance: A tall coast-woman with a weathered face and long sailor's braids threaded with gold.
portrait.dress: A deep blue sea-coat over pale linen, a gold anchor-circlet, a captain's whistle on a chain.
portrait.colours: Sea blue (#1f4a7a), salt gold (#e0c070), sail white (#f0f0e8).

ruler.formerName: Queen Lorvena of Gondolin (characters spec; superseded by the histories)

heir.name: Alod ben Shinah
heir.role: The king's son, who has already captained his own ship to Woqood and back.
heir.succession: The sea crown passes in one line of captains' blood, most often to a king.
heir.portrait: A young sea-captain with braids and a blue coat.

advisors.name: Zahar ben Tamir, Speaker of the Ship-Masters
advisors.office: Speaker of the Council of Ship-Masters
advisors.role: Speaks for the ship-masters who may refuse the queen her ships, and reminds her of it when the price of salt falls.
advisors.portrait: A grey-bearded ship-master with a rope-knot belt.

advisors.name: Yaqir the Harbour-Master
advisors.role: Keeps the harbour of Duum-Saah and the queen's ships ready.
advisors.portrait: A harbour-master with a ledger of hulls and a brass glass.

advisors.name: Alodim ben Melek of the Northern Charts
advisors.role: Keeps the charts of the Kusmeel coast and writes down what the island fishers say, whether the court believes them or not.
advisors.portrait: A man with ink-stained hands over a sea-chart.

commanders.name: Sea-Captain Tamir ben Zarud
commanders.office: Captain of the Sea Crown's Fleet
commanders.role: Commands the queen's fleet on the coast of the Kusmeel.
commanders.portrait: A broad captain in blue with salt in his beard.

commanders.name: Yakam ben Zahud of the Coast Riders
commanders.role: Leads the coast riders and boarders of the landward border that Noris's riders help to guard.
commanders.portrait: A rider in a blue cloak with a spear.

ruler.name: Forge-Prince Telino Barzio
ruler.bio: Telino Barzio, great-grandson of the Nelia Fundo who sealed the Stabilo Pact, rules the Drak Mountains from Castronuro with a council of forge-masters. His forges sell powder-engines and casks to the Stabilo Pact and to any caravan city that can pay, and they guard the recipe that the East learned in the Furnace Year more closely than his treasury. When the Drak Furnace buried the lower forge-town in ash he rebuilt Castronuro higher on the ridge, behind walls that face the mountain as well as the road.

portrait.appearance: A thickset, soot-marked prince with a scarred forearm and a short black beard.
portrait.dress: A leather forge-coat under a mantle of oxblood, an iron circlet, the hammer-seal of House Barzio.

ruler.formerName: King Morod of Drak (characters spec; superseded by the histories)

heir.name: Corino Barzio
heir.role: The Forge-Prince's son, apprenticed to the forge-masters like every Barzio heir before him.
heir.succession: Hereditary in House Barzio, with the forge-masters' assent.
heir.portrait: A young man in a leather apron with a forge-hammer.

advisors.name: Forge-Master Pruno Dolgio
advisors.role: Grandson of Arcan Dolgio, who first compounded the powder and lost two fingers to it; Pruno keeps the recipe in his head, as his grandfather did.
advisors.portrait: A grey forge-master with a burned leather apron and nine fingers.

advisors.name: Arcar Cadarina, Master of the Sulphur Mines
advisors.role: Runs the sulphur workings of the Furnace and the saltpetre caves, and argues with the mountain every day.
advisors.portrait: A soot-faced man with a lamp and a pick.

advisors.name: Tabeo Barzion, Envoy to the Bench
advisors.office: Envoy to the Bench of Houses
advisors.role: Sells Drak's engines to the bench at Postondoroth and collects the Pact's credit before the Prince of the Scales can think of a reason to delay it.
advisors.portrait: A polished envoy in oxblood silk with an engine-model on his desk.

commanders.name: Captain Ferio Barzio of the Engines
commanders.role: The Forge-Prince's cousin, who leads the companies that break gates with Drak's engines.
commanders.portrait: A broad captain in blackened plate beside a powder-engine.

commanders.name: Hardeo Altro of the Ridge
commanders.role: Holds the new walls of Castronuro, which face the mountain as well as the road.
commanders.portrait: A mountain captain in a fur-lined cloak on a high wall.

name: Rhachia
stanceNote: countries.csv has zin_wild_freeholds; an elected tribunes' commonwealth reads as a Free Council. Owner to confirm.

ruler.name: Tribune Alerh of Pordoce
ruler.bio: Alerh of Pordoce was elected tribune by the village heads for seven years, the third tribune since the kiln-towns rose against King Mirodeus and his doubled kiln-tax. He governs the Red Lands and the vent-field of the Rhachia Fires from a kiln-city that is poor, proud and watched. The deposed king's heir waits at Porrenva, the caravan houses still buy his potters' wares, and every spring he refires the clay figure of his first father with the rest of Pordoce.

portrait.appearance: A strong-armed, clay-stained man with cropped dark hair and a level gaze.
portrait.dress: A kiln-father's red-brown apron over plain linen, a tribune's clay seal on a cord.

ruler.formerName: Tribune Arcon Vel (characters spec, for Avalon; superseded by the histories)

heir.note: No heir: the village heads elect a tribune every seven years. The deposed king's heir, Prince Mirodan, lives on a pension at Porrenva and claims the Red Lands.

advisors.name: Alerhan the Kiln-Father
advisors.role: Keeps the kiln-shrines and the Refiring, when every house refires the clay figure of its first father.
advisors.portrait: An old man with clay to the elbows holding a fired figure.

advisors.name: Thaeos of the Clay Pits
advisors.role: Keeps the clay pits the king once seized, and the tally of what the caravan houses pay for the pots.
advisors.portrait: A broad man with a clay-caked spade.

advisors.name: Senis of the Village Heads
advisors.role: Speaks for the village heads who elect the tribune, and remembers the night the gates of Pordoce were opened to them.
advisors.portrait: A white-haired villager with a staff of red clay beads.

commanders.name: Rhoikos of the Slingers
commanders.role: Leads the slingers of the kiln-towns, who rose against the king and would do it again.
commanders.portrait: A clay-stained slinger with a pouch of fired-clay shot.

commanders.name: Alerhios of the Vent-Field
commanders.role: Knows the paths through the Rhachia Fires that a stranger's host would not survive.
commanders.portrait: A soot-faced man with a cloth over his mouth and a spear.

figures.name: Prince Mirodan Furanides
figures.house: Furanides, of the Kings of the Kilns
figures.office: Heir of the deposed Kings of the Kilns
figures.role: The heir of King Mirodeus, who fled the Rising of the Towns; he lives at Porrenva on a pension and has never stopped writing letters to the caravan houses.
figures.portrait: A pale, well-dressed young man in faded red silk.
figures.recruit: A pretender for events and the Rhachia tree; not recruited at the start.

ruler.name: King Keroth Rhanides
ruler.bio: Keroth Rhanides swore at his crowning nine floods ago, as every Rhanid king has sworn, to pay what the mountain asks and to keep the seven forts. He holds the southern mountains, the river and the dry Kalioth upland from Atonto, and his mines are rich and his forts manned with miners who are also soldiers. Every spring he pays the fire-tithe to the mountain, which his people call a tax and his priests an offering, and he has never once been late.

portrait.appearance: A hard, broad-shouldered mountain king with painted eyes and a grey-streaked beard.
portrait.dress: A miner's leather under a gold collar, a crown of iron set with river gold, a seven-towered badge.
portrait.colours: River gold (#c9a24a), flood blue (#2f5f8a), reed green (#4a7a4a).

heir.name: Prince Kerios Rhanides
heir.role: The king's son, who has served a winter in each of the seven forts.
heir.succession: Hereditary in the Rhanides; each king swears at his crowning to pay the tithe and keep the forts.
heir.portrait: A young prince in a miner's coat with a gold collar.

advisors.name: Alerh of the Fire-Tithe
advisors.role: Carries the fire-tithe up the Smoking Teeth each spring and comes back down, which is the main thing his office requires.
advisors.portrait: A soot-robed priest with a brazier of offerings.

advisors.name: Morodis, Master of the Mines
advisors.role: Keeps the rich mines of the southern mountains and the loans the caravan houses make against their ore.
advisors.portrait: A heavy man in a fur-lined coat with a lump of ore.

advisors.name: Castellan Esiuris of the Seven Forts
advisors.role: Keeps the seven forts of the Kalioth upland manned against the ogres of the heights and the raiders of the Gold Road.
advisors.portrait: A grizzled castellan in iron with a ring of fort keys.

commanders.name: Captain Esiuron of the Kalioth
commanders.role: Holds the upland forts and has fought more ogres than any man in the East.
commanders.portrait: A scarred fort-captain with a long spear and a miner's lamp.

commanders.name: Alerhan of the Miner Companies
commanders.role: Leads the miners who are also soldiers, and keeps their picks sharp for either work.
commanders.portrait: A sturdy man with a pick and a short sword.

ruler.name: Prince Blosian Plutides
ruler.bio: Blosian Plutides is in the fourth Rising of his reign over the southern valley, and he keeps the upland of the Blozan Lands as his own estate. Plutondo is rich in ash-grown grain and ore and the Gold Road begins at its quays, but it lies deep in Stabilo's ledgers since the Vent Year, when the Plutondo Vents killed the harvest and the caravan houses bought the princedom's debts. He resents the houses that fed his people more than the vents that starved them, and says so at every banquet.

portrait.appearance: A young, restless prince with painted eyes and a quick temper in his face.
portrait.dress: A white robe with a gold collar, an ash-grey mantle, the river-crown of the Plutides.
portrait.colours: River gold (#c9a24a), flood blue (#2f5f8a), reed green (#4a7a4a).

ruler.formerName: Prince Blozan (characters spec; named after a place and renamed by the histories)
ruler.note: Shares his given name with Blosian Furanides, the historical first Quay-Master of Luv-zhise (a figure of the histories, not a character).

heir.name: Alerheus Plutides
heir.role: The prince's younger brother, who thinks the debts should be paid rather than shouted about, and is popular with the caravan houses for it.
heir.portrait: A calm young man in white linen with a ledger.

advisors.name: Fulio Prudon, Agent of the Caravan Houses
advisors.role: Holds the princedom's grain debts for the Stabilo houses, and attends every banquet at which he is insulted.
advisors.portrait: A smooth Stabilic merchant in jade silk.

advisors.name: Alerh of the Ash Fields
advisors.role: Keeps the ash-grown grain and the ore of the southern valley, and the count of every bushel the Vent Year cost.
advisors.portrait: A farmer-man with grey ash on his sleeves and a grain-measure.

advisors.name: Ernoith the Vent-Watcher
advisors.role: Watches the vents and writes down every breath they take, and was the only man who warned of the Vent Year.
advisors.portrait: An old scholar with a smoke-stained robe and a wax tablet.

commanders.name: Captain Morodian of the Valley Host
commanders.role: Commands the valley's chariots and archers.
commanders.portrait: A captain in a bronze corselet with a chariot-whip.

commanders.name: Alerhan of the Blozan Upland
commanders.role: Keeps the prince's upland estate and its herdsmen-archers.
commanders.portrait: A man in a herder's cloak with a bow.

ruler.name: King Ernoian Ostorides
ruler.bio: Ernoian Ostorides, lake-king of Ohitus, rules the north-east lakes and the counties of Ernois, Grova and Nethnu, whose counts still carry his lantern at the Lantern Float. His highland kingdom keeps the Reckoning of the Twelve so that its merchants share one calendar with the west, and it lives on the cedar, fish and lanterns of the Lake Road, which both great powers claim. The Lantern Peace with Mora has held for longer than any lake-reader expected, and he means it to hold for his whole reign.

portrait.appearance: A tall, lake-tanned highland king with a long grey-black beard and gentle eyes.
portrait.dress: A cedar-green robe over pale linen, a lantern-crown of silver, a carved cedar staff.
portrait.colours: Lake blue (#5a8aa8), lantern pale (#d8d4c4), cedar green (#3f5f4a).

ruler.formerName: King Ocellio of Ostoroth (characters spec; superseded by the histories)
ruler.note: His given name echoes the county of Ernois; kept because the Alerhic stem ernoi is in the language data and the histories use it.

heir.name: Prince Kersion Ostorides
heir.role: The king's son, who carried the lantern at the Float for the first time this year and did not drop it.
heir.portrait: A young prince in cedar-green with a lantern.

advisors.name: Count Lorveos of Grova
advisors.role: Eldest of the three counts who carry the king's lantern, and the one who carries it highest.
advisors.portrait: An old count in a fur-trimmed robe with a silver lantern.

advisors.name: Alerh the Lake-Reader
advisors.role: Reads the lakes along the Lake Road, which keep the memory of the caravans, and leads the merchants and fishers in prayer at the water.
advisors.portrait: A man in lake-blue at the water's edge with a floating lamp.

advisors.name: Alerhion, Master of the Cedar
advisors.role: Sells the cedar and the lanterns of the highlands to the west, and has never sold either to a power that claimed the Lake Road.
advisors.portrait: A merchant with a cedar plank and a lantern sample.

commanders.name: Captain Nethan of Nethnu
commanders.role: Leads the boat archers and highland bowmen of the counties.
commanders.portrait: A highland captain in a cedar-green cloak with a long bow.

commanders.name: Alerhan of the Lake Boats
commanders.role: Commands the boats on the Hot Lake that keep to the line of the hot shallows that the Lantern Peace set.
commanders.portrait: A boat-captain in a lake-blue cloak with a lantern at the bow.

ruler.name: Speaker Alerh of Eraver
ruler.bio: Alerh of Eraver was chosen Speaker by the council of the lake towns for three years, the first from Eraver since that coast town joined the council. He governs the Hot Lake's east shore, the Mora coast and Eraver from Gonnois, and his realm is the granary of the East and the most peaceful of its realms, with no king and no wish for one. Every power that wants to feed a host in the East must buy his grain, and he makes sure they pay for it.

portrait.appearance: A lake-tanned, broad-faced man with grey eyes and a farmer's strong hands.
portrait.dress: A pale linen gown with a sheaf-brooch, a blue lake-cloak, the Speaker's chain of grain-ears in silver.
portrait.colours: Lake blue (#5a8aa8), lantern pale (#d8d4c4), cedar green (#3f5f4a).

ruler.formerName: Speaker Moira Eraver (characters spec; superseded by the histories)
ruler.note: His given name is close to the Woqood district of Lorvens; kept as the histories name him.

heir.note: No heir: the council of the lake towns chooses a Speaker every three years.
heir.succession: Elective, three years (the lake towns' council).

advisors.name: Alerhan of the Granaries
advisors.office: Keeper of the Granaries of Gonnois
advisors.role: Keeps the granaries of the East's best farmland, and knows to the sack what each power has bought and what it still owes.
advisors.portrait: A sturdy man with a grain-measure and a ledger.

advisors.name: Ernoios of the Salt Pans
advisors.role: Reads the lake at the hot shallows and says that something under it breathed out in the month the lake boiled over the salt pans.
advisors.portrait: A gaunt lake-reader in a damp grey robe with a lamp.

advisors.name: Alerheus of Gonnois
advisors.office: Elder of the Lake Towns' Council
advisors.role: Eldest of the council of the lake towns, who has seen a dozen Speakers come and go and liked most of them.
advisors.portrait: An old man in pale linen with a staff of reeds.

commanders.name: Furaneus of the Fisheries
commanders.role: Commands the armed fishery boats that held the east shore in the Lakeshore Quarrel.
commanders.portrait: A fisher-captain with a net-hook and a lake-blue cloak.

commanders.name: Alerhios of the Town Militia
commanders.role: Leads the militia of the lake towns, who drill at harvest-fairs and are better at loading grain than at fighting.
commanders.portrait: A man in a leather jerkin with a spear and a grain-sack badge.

ruler.name: King Esiuran Fosocides
ruler.bio: Esiuran Fosocides rules the Delbiz Grasslands and the Fosoco from the fair town of Furtonlin, of the line that married the heiress of the Fosoco lordship and took the river's name. The herds have recovered since the Great Murrain killed two in three of them, and the horse-fair is again the richest in the East. The old quarrel with Alerhia sleeps under a marriage treaty, and the caravan houses that lent after the Murrain expect to be repaid in horses, which he pays them slowly and in the poorer ones.

portrait.appearance: A lean, wind-burnt grassland king with painted eyes and a horseman's bow legs.
portrait.dress: A riding robe of gold and blue, a horse-headed gold collar, a crown of plaited gold wire.
portrait.colours: River gold (#c9a24a), flood blue (#2f5f8a), reed green (#4a7a4a).

heir.name: Prince Fosian Fosocides
heir.role: The king's son, who rides better than he reads and is betrothed by treaty to a daughter of Alerhia.
heir.portrait: A boy on a fine grey horse in a gold-and-blue coat.

advisors.name: Alerh, Master of the Horse-Fair
advisors.role: Runs the richest horse-fair in the East and knows every buyer's purse before he reaches the pens.
advisors.portrait: A sharp-eyed horse-trader with a coiled whip.

advisors.name: Rhanis of the Herds
advisors.role: Rebuilt the herds after the Murrain from breeding stock bought on credit, and still counts the debt.
advisors.portrait: An old horse-master with a halter and a weathered face.

advisors.name: Cormo Cerano, Agent of the Houses
advisors.role: Represents the caravan houses that lent after the Murrain, and inspects every horse the king pays them with.
advisors.portrait: A Stabilic merchant in amber with a tally of horses.

commanders.name: Captain Furanis of the Grass Riders
commanders.role: Leads the horse-lords' riders, who broke from Alerhia's service at the Horse-Fair Oath and have been proud of it since.
commanders.portrait: A rider in a scale coat with a long lance.

commanders.name: Alerhan of the Fosoco
commanders.role: Keeps the river lordship that came to the crown with the Fosoco groom.
commanders.portrait: A man rider in blue with a spear.

name: Kersian
stanceNote: countries.csv has zin_wild_freeholds; a free city under a market council reads as a Free Council. Owner to confirm.

ruler.name: Lantern-Warden Alerh Kersides
ruler.bio: Alerh Kersides holds the lantern this year, chosen by the market council of guilds and lantern-wardens to speak for Osrale, a free city of the Lake Road that neither Noris nor Stabilo may garrison. His city is rich, small and anxious, kept free by the rivalry of two powers and taxing both their caravans alike. When the caravanserai district burned, both powers sent money to rebuild it and the council spent each gift on a separate wall, which he thinks the wisest thing it has ever done.

portrait.appearance: A quick-eyed, slender man with Aenoran-fair skin and dark hair, of a family that follows the news from Parim.
portrait.dress: A lake-blue gown with a guild collar, the treaty lantern of Osrale carried in one hand.
portrait.colours: Lake blue (#5a8aa8), lantern pale (#d8d4c4), cedar green (#3f5f4a).

heir.note: No heir: the market council chooses a Lantern-Warden each year.

advisors.name: Blosis Vikias, Master of the Guilds
advisors.role: Speaks for the guilds of the market and the caravanserai, and taxes Noris and Stabilo alike, to the penny.
advisors.portrait: A plump guildsman with a scale and a seal.

advisors.name: Velmec Parel of the Aenoran Families
advisors.role: Speaks for the Aenoran-descended families of Osrale and reads every letter from Parim before the council does.
advisors.portrait: A man in Aenoran blue with a packet of letters.

advisors.name: Alerheus of the Cistern
advisors.role: Keeps the cistern where the first lantern of the Lantern Peace was floated, and the Lake Litany beside it.
advisors.portrait: An old man in pale blue with a floating lantern.

commanders.name: Captain Furanoth of the Walls
commanders.role: Keeps the two new walls that the rival gifts built.
commanders.portrait: A wall-captain with a lantern-badge and a spear.

commanders.name: Alerhios of the Lantern-Wardens
commanders.role: Leads the lantern-wardens who keep the night watch of the market.
commanders.portrait: A young warden with a lantern on a pole.

name: Mostok
stanceNote: countries.csv has zin_wild_freeholds; a free city under a weighers' council reads as a Free Council. Owner to confirm.

ruler.name: First Weigher Milio Crovo
ruler.bio: Milio Crovo is First Weigher of Cereosa for this year, chosen by the weighers who keep the city's honest scale and govern it besides. The junction city lives on inns, storage and weighing, both great powers keep envoys there, and the war of Noris and Stabilo ended in its hall. He knows that Cereosa's freedom lasts exactly as long as Noris and Stabilo distrust each other, and he does what he can to keep them at it.

portrait.appearance: An olive-skinned, round-faced weigher with a short grey beard and spectacles of polished crystal.
portrait.dress: A black weigher's robe with a bronze scale embroidered on the breast, a set of brass weights at his belt.

heir.note: No heir: the weighers' council chooses a First Weigher each year.

advisors.name: Arcar Cerio, Master of the Caravanserai
advisors.role: Keeps the inns and the warehouses of the junction, and emptied them for a year when Stabilo demanded its bronze be weighed free.
advisors.portrait: A broad innkeeper-man with a ring of warehouse keys.

advisors.name: Plerano Tablia, Keeper of the Envoys' House
advisors.role: Lodges the envoys of Noris and Stabilo in the same house and makes sure they meet at breakfast.
advisors.portrait: A genial host in a black coat with a tray of cups.

advisors.name: Weigher Arcino Fundia
advisors.role: Keeps the honest scale in the hall and the weights against which every caravan's are checked.
advisors.portrait: A stern man beside a great bronze scale.

commanders.name: Captain Tabino Belano of the Scale Guard
commanders.role: Commands the small guard of the junction city, which keeps the peace among caravaneers rather than any army.
commanders.portrait: A guard-captain in bronze scale with a crossbow.

commanders.name: Arcio of the Four Roads
commanders.role: Keeps the road junctions open and the caravans moving through them.
commanders.portrait: A mounted road-warden with a horn.

ruler.name: Mylana Azano, Head of the House

title.english: Lady of Ceralon, Head of the House of Azano

ruler.bio: Mylana Azano has headed the house that owns Ceralon since her father's death in 4A 1739, and as head of the house she is the city's lord by charter. Her ledgers record loans to half the courts of the East, her bench-cousins in Postondoroth resent her freedom, and her bronze-roofed house over the market was built with the winnings of her father's silk wager. She keeps the city independent by charter rather than by arms, and she would rather lend to an army than raise one.

portrait.appearance: A young, olive-skinned woman with a merchant's cool gaze and a high, jewelled coiffure.
portrait.dress: A gown of amber and oxblood silk, a jewelled collar, the house mark of Azano in gold at her breast.

ruler.note: House Azano owns the city named for it; the name is the house's, not a place-name given to the ruler.

heir.name: Myleo Azano
heir.office: Brother of the Head of the House
heir.role: Mylana's younger brother, who keeps the house's second ledger and would head the house if she fell.
heir.succession: The head of the house names the heir; the charter passes with the headship.
heir.portrait: A young merchant in amber silk with a ledger.

advisors.name: Posano Prudia, Keeper of the Ledgers
advisors.role: Keeps the ledgers of the loans to half the courts of the East, and remembers the Ledger Feud with the Prudos better than anyone.
advisors.portrait: An old clerk with ink-stained fingers and a stack of ledgers.

advisors.name: Arcar Azanon, Master of the Silk
advisors.role: Runs the silk trade from the South Lands that built the bronze-roofed house.
advisors.portrait: A man in shimmering silk with a bolt of cloth.

advisors.name: Crovio the Quiet
advisors.role: Keeps the door of the house, which in the Ledger Feud meant keeping hired knives out of it.
advisors.portrait: A lean man in grey with a knife he never draws in company.

commanders.name: Captain Arcanio Fulio of the House Guard
commanders.role: Commands the hired guard of the house, which is paid well enough not to be bought by anyone else.
commanders.portrait: A guard-captain in bronze with the Azano mark on his shield.

commanders.name: Arceo of the Market Quay
commanders.role: Commands the house's two armed galleys that escort its cargoes along the coast.
commanders.portrait: A galley-captain in amber with a brass whistle.

ruler.name: Chief Factor Narino Shindo
ruler.bio: Narino Shindo was chosen Chief Factor for life by the council of timber and gum factors who govern Kerdoco, the jungle-edge city that bought its freedom from its houses. The town lives by the Stabilo Pact's need for hardwood and sealed casks, and its gum seals Drak's powder casks under the Gum Charter. He keeps the Ledger Count like the old houses and fears the jungle's fevers more than any army, since a fever once killed half the town and made it move to the higher ground.

portrait.appearance: A lean, sallow factor with a fever-thin face and sharp eyes.
portrait.dress: A light linen robe against the heat, a wide hat, the factors' seal of jungle gum on a cord.

heir.note: No heir: the council of factors chooses the next Chief Factor for life.
heir.succession: Elective for life (the council of factors).

advisors.name: Arcar Ciro, Master of the Gum
advisors.role: Keeps the gum grounds and the contract with Drak.
advisors.portrait: A sunburnt man with sticky hands and a gum-pot.

advisors.name: Doctor Belmio Narco
advisors.role: Keeps the town's fever-house and the records of the year half the town died.
advisors.portrait: A gaunt physician with a herb-bag and a mask of cloth.

advisors.name: Ferrano of the Timber
advisors.role: Cuts and floats the hardwood the Pact's shipwrights need.
advisors.portrait: A broad woodsman with an axe and a hardwood log.

commanders.name: Captain Arcolo of the Jungle Edge
commanders.role: Leads the guards who keep the timber and gum grounds safe from the jungle.
commanders.portrait: A captain in light leather with a machete-like blade.

commanders.name: Arcio of the Floats
commanders.role: Keeps the timber floats moving down to the coast.
commanders.portrait: A man on a log raft with a pole.

ruler.name: First Warden Pelio Shindo
ruler.bio: Pelio Shindo is First Warden of the council that the guilds of Nerhuus elect to collect the fire-tithe and carry it up the mountain. His city of the caravan princes lies in the shadow of Mount Ergo, where the people say a devil once took a whole caravan and left only its scales laid out on a scorched stone. The council of 4A 1502 decided the tithe was a superstition, and in the autumn the upper town burned; Nerhuus has paid every year since, and Pelio carries the first sack up himself.

portrait.appearance: A soot-browned, nervous man with singed eyebrows and a careful smile.
portrait.dress: A fire-proof leather cloak over amber silk, a tithe-warden's brass key, a scale-badge.

ruler.note: Cousin of Narino Shindo of Obmi in the same great house (proposed).

heir.note: No heir: the guilds elect the tithe-wardens and the wardens choose their First Warden.

advisors.name: Nelo the Tithe-Bearer
advisors.role: Leads the procession that carries the tithe to the scorched stone, and has come back every time.
advisors.portrait: A grey man in a soot-black robe with a sack of offerings.

advisors.name: Arcar Arcon, Speaker of the Guilds
advisors.role: Speaks for the guilds that elect the wardens and trade with everyone, because the city cannot afford an enemy.
advisors.portrait: A shrewd man with a guild chain and a purse.

advisors.name: Corneo Seno, Keeper of the Scales
advisors.role: Keeps the scales of the vanished caravan in the guild hall and the city's treasury beside them.
advisors.portrait: An old clerk beside a set of blackened scales.

commanders.name: Captain Bellino Telan of the Mountain Road
commanders.role: Guards the mountain road and refuses to go past the scorched stone.
commanders.portrait: A captain in bronze scale on a dark mountain road.

commanders.name: Arcio of the Upper Town
commanders.office: Captain of the Upper Town Watch
commanders.role: Keeps the watch in the rebuilt upper town and its fire-buckets always full.
commanders.portrait: A young man with a bucket and a spear.

name: Woqood
stanceNote: countries.csv has zin_wild_freeholds; a league of sealers' clans under a clan-moot reads as Clan Moot. Owner to confirm.

ruler.name: Harpoon-Speaker Alodim ben Nurek
ruler.bio: Alodim bat Nurek of the Meli boat holds the harpoon this winter, chosen by the clan-moot of Pehami from the boat clans to speak for the snow coast, Cream and Lorvens. His sealers, harpooners and sled-men trade furs, seal-fat and ivory with Naamis and the Lake Road and keep to themselves. The moot has kept peace with the sea crown since the Ice Winter, when the clans crossed the frozen sea and Naamis fed them, and he will stay out of any eastern war unless someone attacks his coast.

portrait.appearance: A broad, wind-reddened man with black braids and narrow, laughing eyes.
portrait.dress: A sealskin parka trimmed with white fur, an ivory harpoon of office, bone beads at the throat.
portrait.colours: Snow white (#e8f0f0), sea slate (#3a5a6a), seal-blood red (#8a2a2a).

heir.note: No heir: the clan-moot chooses a Harpoon-Speaker from the boat clans each winter.

advisors.name: Melim of the Seal Grounds
advisors.role: Divides the seal grounds among the boat clans each spring, and is Yarun's uncle, which nobody has ever held against him.
advisors.portrait: An old sealer with a scarred face and a walrus-ivory staff.

advisors.name: Alod ben Tumud of the Fur Trade
advisors.role: Sells the furs, fat and ivory to Naamis and the Lake Road.
advisors.portrait: A man in a fur cloak with a bale of white pelts.

advisors.name: Barak the Ice-Reader
advisors.role: Reads the sea-ice and says when it will hold a sled and when it will not.
advisors.portrait: A squinting old man with an ice-staff on a frozen shore.

commanders.name: Tumak of the Harpooners
commanders.role: Leads the harpooners and sled-men who could fight on the ice if anyone were foolish enough to come.
commanders.portrait: A sealer with a long harpoon and a sled-dog.

commanders.name: Alodiq of the Boat Clans
commanders.role: Leads the skin-boats of the clans along the snow coast.
commanders.portrait: A man in a skin-boat with a paddle and a harpoon.

ruler.name: Barim ben Yaqud, Lord of the Boats

title.english: Lord of the Boats of Orato

ruler.bio: Barim ben Yaqud rules Orato and Fladev from the stone harbour of Nodoqood, two small isles of fishers facing the Kusmeel, as his family has since the boats accepted the first lord. Four years ago his fishermen said they had seen black ships moving among the black islands of the north without lights or oars, and he sent word to Duum-Saah and Furvior, and no court believed them. The fishermen have stopped talking about it in the market, and some of them have stopped fishing the northern grounds, and Barim has not told them they are wrong.

portrait.appearance: A weathered, grey-bearded fisher-lord with salt-cracked hands and wary eyes.
portrait.dress: A heavy oiled sea-cloak, a fisherman's knitted cap, a silver boat-badge.

heir.name: Yaqud ben Barim
heir.role: The lord's son, named for his grandfather, who has fished the northern grounds since he could hold a line.
heir.succession: The lordship passes in one fishing family when the boats accept the heir.
heir.portrait: A young fisher with a net over his shoulder.

advisors.name: Alod of Fladev
advisors.role: Headman of the eastern isle that joined the lordship by a wedding, and the lord's cousin by the same wedding.
advisors.portrait: A sturdy fisher-man with a gutting knife and a shawl.

advisors.name: Barzud the Harbour-Keeper
advisors.role: Keeps the stone harbour and the boats, and counts every one that comes back.
advisors.portrait: An old harbour-keeper with a coil of rope.

advisors.name: Nurim the Teller
advisors.role: The fisherman who first told of the black ships, and who still keeps watch from the north cape when the others will not.
advisors.portrait: A fisherman on a cliff staring at a grey sea.
advisors.note: His tale stays a disputed fishermen's tale until zin_zol_rising (V10).

commanders.name: Yakar of the Fishing Fleet
commanders.role: Leads the fishing fleet when it is armed, which has never yet happened.
commanders.portrait: A fisher-captain at the tiller of a broad boat.

commanders.name: Alodo ben Yaqud of the Isle Guard
commanders.role: The lord's brother, who keeps the isle guard of fishers with spears.
commanders.portrait: A man with a fish-spear on a stone quay.
